review_notes:
I read the whole file. It already bundles the structure the rubric would ask for. `coderivations` is a submodule of the endomorphisms, and `coderivEquivTaylor` is a linear equivalence onto the Taylor components, with `_apply` and `_symm_apply` simp lemmas. `IsCoderivation` stays a Prop, which fits a predicate on endomorphisms. The twisted lemma `eq_of_letter_comp_eq_of_twist` is shared on purpose with the graded variant, so I did not treat it as a missing structure.

One candidate: `LinearMap.taylorComponent` is unbundled, and its `taylorComponent_zero`, `taylorComponent_add` and `taylorComponent_smul` lemmas are really the fields of a linear map from the endomorphisms into families of arity components. A grep of the repo shows only `taylorComponent_zero` has consumers, one in this file and one in AInfinity/Coderivation.lean. `taylorComponent_add` and `taylorComponent_smul` have none. Bundling would therefore not simplify any existing consumer, and `taylorComponent` is already a named operation with a simple definition. I judged this optional packaging, not a clear improvement, and did not report it.

I did not find any other missing bundle or any circular-dependency concern. The remaining uncertainty is that I only grepped for `taylorComponent` uses and did not read every downstream file.
